item.title: Draymond Green returns to Golden State for $27M after Warriors' pursuit of LeBron James falls flat
item.description: Draymond Green's opt-out was designed to clear cap space for LeBron James, but after James chose Philadelphia, Golden State paid the exact same price.
item.content:encoded:
Draymond Green is staying put, and it cost the Golden State Warriors exactly what it would've cost them all along.

The 36-year-old is returning on a one-year, $27.7 million contract, according to Klutch Sports.

Back in June, Green declined his original $27.7 million player option to help Golden State create cap space for a run at LeBron James. The Warriors believed they had a legitimate shot at pairing James with Stephen Curry.

LEBRON JAMES MAKES NBA FREE AGENCY DECISION, ANNOUNCES PLANS TO SIGN WITH 76ERS

Instead, James chose Philadelphia, signing a two-year deal with the 76ers. Golden State's LeBron gamble failed, leaving the Warriors right back where they started with Green.

The deal does not include a no-trade clause. It also pushes Golden State over the first apron, limiting the Warriors to veteran minimum additions while preserving future cap flexibility.

Both Green and James are represented by Rich Paul and Klutch Sports. Green's opt-out gave Golden State its cleanest path to LeBron while leaving the Warriors with virtually no realistic scenario in which they could turn around and offer him less if the recruiting pitch failed.

Once LeBron picked Philadelphia, re-signing Green became the obvious move. General manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. had even less incentive to alienate a franchise cornerstone after missing on James, especially after reports last season linked Green to trade discussions with Milwaukee.

The one concession Dunleavy secured was keeping the deal to a single year. Green isn't the athlete he was during Golden State's dynasty years. The shorter contract preserves future flexibility while avoiding a longer commitment to an aging star.

The Warriors get their emotional enforcer and defensive anchor back, but they're still paying premium money for a roster that looks well past its championship window.

They cleared cap space chasing LeBron, struck out, then circled back and paid Green exactly what he would've earned anyway.

Sometimes the biggest move of the offseason is paying for the one that never happened.

item.title: WNBA media predictably embarrasses itself again by ignoring Sophie Cunningham story over All-Star Weekend
item.description: WNBA reporters had access to 22 All-Stars and Cathy Engelbert in Chicago but never asked about Sophie Cunningham's transgender athlete stance.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA media had every opportunity to show it could cover the league like a serious professional sport over All-Star Weekend in Chicago.

It blew it.

Reporters had access to the league’s biggest players and Commissioner Cathy Engelbert just days after Sophie Cunningham said biological males should not compete in girls' and women's sports. Yet not one public answer emerged from the weekend about whether the league’s stars agreed with her.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

The outcome was, sadly, predictable.

Before the event, I wrote on X:

It did not.

One important disclosure: OutKick and Fox News Digital attempted to cover All-Star Weekend in person, and I planned to ask the players and Commissioner Cathy Engelbert about Cunningham’s comments (if given the chance). We applied for a credential through the NBA/WNBA credential portal, but the league denied the request because it was submitted 10 days after its June 16 deadline.

The portal was still open and accepted the application, which was submitted four weeks prior to the event.

I had not received the WNBA’s original credential advisory or either of the two reminder emails the league said it sent. We asked the league to reconsider, noting that OutKick and Fox News Digital were approved to cover last year's All-Star Game, but the WNBA stood by its decision.

So, no, OutKick did not ask the players in Chicago because we didn't have access to do so.

That left the job to the reporters who received credentials.

After reviewing the publicly available press conferences, interview videos, transcripts and coverage from All-Star Weekend, I could not find one instance of a WNBA All-Star or Commissioner Cathy Engelbert being asked about Cunningham’s statement.

Cunningham’s comments came in an ESPN profile published just before the All-Star break.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’" Cunningham said. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

Reporters grilled Cunningham just before the break. She did not retreat.

"I said what I said. I think it’s kinda common sense," Cunningham said.

The story quickly moved beyond Cunningham.

Las Vegas Aces forward Brianna Turner publicly defended transgender participation in women’s sports. The White House backed Cunningham. The Associated Press identified the transgender-athlete debate as one of the major cultural issues hanging over All-Star Weekend.

In other words, this wasn't an obscure social media controversy that reporters could credibly claim they hadn't seen.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SEES SUPPORT SURGE AFTER STAR PUTS CAREER ON LINE FOR GIRLS SPORTS

An active WNBA player had taken a clear position on one of the biggest debates in women’s sports. Her comments drew a response from another player and reached the White House. The league’s most prominent athletes were about to gather in the same city for several days of media availability.

The questions practically wrote themselves.

Do you agree with Cunningham?

Should women’s sports be reserved for biological females?

Do Cunningham’s comments conflict with the values of the WNBA?

Apparently, that was too much to ask.

The WNBA assembled 22 All-Stars in Chicago, including Caitlin Clark, A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart, Paige Bueckers and Cunningham’s Indiana Fever teammates Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston. Players participated in practice interviews, informal scrums and official press conferences throughout the weekend.

There is always a chance that a reporter asked someone about Cunningham during a scrum that was not recorded or published. It is impossible to prove that the topic never came up once over the weekend.

But journalism is not a private conversation between a reporter and an athlete. The point is to provide information to the public.

No outlet appears to have produced an answer from an All-Star. No videos surfaced, no quote appeared in a story and no reporter posted a player’s response on social media.

If someone asked, the answer apparently was not important enough to publish. The practical result is the same.

The public still has no idea what the WNBA’s most prominent players think about trans-identifying biological males competing in women's sports and using women's locker rooms.

The irony is that All-Star Weekend included the inaugural WNBA Media & Innovation Summit. The event’s stated theme was "From Participation to Power," and organizers promoted it as a discussion about who will shape the future of women’s sports.

Evidently, asking female athletes whether women’s sports should be reserved for females didn't fit the program.

The failure to question Engelbert was particularly glaring.

The commissioner began her All-Star press conference by addressing racism, misogyny, homophobia, harassment and threats against players. She said the league is built on "inclusion and respect" and pledged to make every player feel safe and supported.

That provided a natural opening to ask about Cunningham.

Does the commissioner believe Cunningham’s comments are consistent with the WNBA’s values?

What is the league’s position on transgender eligibility?

Does Engelbert believe supporting a female-only athletic category is exclusionary?

No one asked.

Instead, reporters questioned Engelbert about the new replay center, international games, the Las Vegas Aces investigation, the relationship between the league and its players, officiating, security, her future as commissioner, coaching diversity, HBCU internships and her communication style.

Several were legitimate questions. The problem is not that reporters asked about officiating or league operations. The problem is that the full press conference ended without anyone addressing the controversy involving one of Engelbert’s players.

Engelbert even talked about young girls viewing WNBA players as role models.

Cunningham’s entire argument was that young girls deserve protection in locker rooms and athletic competition. Still, no one in the room made the connection. Or, possibly, no one in the room wanted to make the connection.

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

Some reporters had plenty to say about Cunningham. They just didn’t appear interested in asking WNBA players about her.

The Guardian published an All-Star Weekend feature that characterized Cunningham’s comments as "transphobic language." The story included fresh quotes from Courtney Williams, Becky Hammon, Jessica Shepard and A’ja Wilson on other subjects.

Yet the published article contained no response from any of them about Cunningham’s comments.

That captures the problem with much of the media covering this league.

A reporter was comfortable delivering a moral judgment about Cunningham’s statement. Getting a prominent WNBA player on the record about that statement was apparently less important.

The Associated Press also included the controversy in its scene-setting story from Chicago. But the article relied on Cunningham’s previous ESPN quote and Turner’s social media comments rather than producing a response from an All-Star attending the weekend.

The media knew it was a story. They wrote about it. They just decided not to do any actual reporting.

None of this should be surprising.

In 2024, Caitlin Clark went through a massive media tour before entering the WNBA. Reporters asked her the same safe questions repeatedly, but no one asked the most influential young woman in American sports what she thought about transgender athletes competing against females.

Later that year, USA Today reporter Christine Brennan asked DiJonai Carrington whether she intentionally poked Clark in the eye. It was a completely reasonable question about something that happened during a basketball game.

The WNBA Players’ Association responded by calling on USA Today to discipline Brennan and suggesting that she should lose access.

Then came the Brittney Griner controversy last season. A viral video showed Griner saying something after fouling out against the Indiana Fever. Many viewers believed she made a racially charged remark.

For nearly three weeks, no WNBA reporter asked Griner what she said. OutKick sought credentials specifically to ask the question and was denied by multiple teams before the Washington Mystics eventually granted access.

When we finally asked Griner, she denied using the phrase attributed to her. The controversy largely died because an athlete finally answered the actual question.

That should have been a lesson for everyone covering the league.

Instead, All-Star Weekend showed that nothing has changed.

The WNBA and its players say they want the attention, revenue and stature afforded to major professional sports leagues. That comes with real media coverage. Sometimes athletes have to answer questions they would rather avoid.

A reporter didn't have to agree with Sophie Cunningham to ask about her comments. In fact, anyone who believed her statement was offensive or harmful had an even stronger reason to ask other players for their views.

OutKick sought access because we intended to ask.

The league denied our credential request, and the reporters who were admitted apparently decided the answer was better left unknown.

The WNBA and its media cheerleaders spent All-Star Weekend celebrating the growth of women’s sports while avoiding the most basic question about who should be allowed to compete in them.

item.title: Ex-FDA commissioner confronted on 'outrageous' Fauci diaries by CNBC host
item.description: Scott Gottlieb called Dr. Anthony Fauci's diary entries "disappointing," citing evidence of suppressing opinions and enjoying media notoriety during the COVID-19 pandemic.
item.content:encoded:
Scott Gottlieb, a former FDA commissioner, was confronted about former National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director Anthony Fauci's diaries on Monday in a back-and-forth on CNBC, which host Joe Kernen called "outrageous."

"How about your buddy Fauci, that I've asked you about in the past. You've defended him quite a bit," Kernen said. "I've asked about whether he orchestrated a cover-up of the lab origin because of his involvement in making gain-of-function research possible again in China, which he did. He knew that would come back to haunt him and then basically told his colleagues go with the natural origin. It was obvious three years ago, Scott, to me anyway, and everybody else, that he orchestrated that."

Fauci’s diary entries were released on Saturday by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., detailing the doctor’s role during the COVID-19 crisis through conversations with President Donald Trump, governors, world leaders, media appearances and his personal observations as the pandemic unfolded in 2020.

"Well look, and I've looked through the emails, some of them have been online, I think it's disappointing to see him trying to suppress alternative opinions, and that clearly was evidence from the emails. I thought it was disappointing. The part of it that also disappointed me was how much he enjoyed the media associated with the event and his own appearances," Gotlieb said.

ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN AND MS NOW IGNORE FAUCI DIARY ENTRIES THAT REVEAL FIXATION ON FAME DURING COVID

"I think a lot of us went on to media out of a sense of obligation," he continued. "It was a hard time for all of us. I know it was a hard time for you. I think a lot of us felt an obligation to inform the public. And it wasn't particularly enjoyable. I mean, I got a lot of threats, others did as well, associated with that, and so to see those emails where he is evidencing some pleasure in the notoriety that he achieved, that's disappointing."

Kernen pushed back and said it was "outrageous."

"Does having a reputation totally in the toilet at 85 years, does that hold him to account for what he was responsible for?" Kernen asked.

Gottlieb said the Fauci he knew over the years was not the one he saw in the emails, and said the former NIH head was always careful and thoughtful.

Kernen specifically brought up Fauci's relationship with members of the liberal media. Fauci’s closest media ally appeared to have been CNN anchor Jake Tapper, who was mentioned 41 times in the diary.

FAUCI'S DIARY SHOWS HE FED QUESTIONS TO JOURNALISTS, BUILT FRIENDSHIPS WITH MEDIA FIGURES

"Did you figure out the obsession with mainstream media in defending him and Jake Tapper having multiple dinners and best friends? What did that come from? And I know people around here that would call Tony Fauci a hero," Kernen said.

Gottlieb said he couldn't dissect the relationship, but again said he was disappointed by the emails.

Fauci did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

According to the diary, Tapper texted Fauci to mock rival cable news hosts and other doctors. On one occasion, Tapper called to check on Fauci after an appearance on his show irked Trump supporters.

"Jake wanted to make sure the interview did not cause me any problems," Fauci wrote on April 13, 2020.

EXCLUSIVE: BIDEN PARDON WON'T SHIELD FAUCI IF HE LIES TO CONGRESS, COMER SAYS

In July 2020, Fauci gushed that he was forming a friendship with Tapper.

"Had dinner over Jake Tapper and Jen Tapper’s home in DC. Terrific couple. Friendship building," Fauci wrote, according to the diary.

Later that month, Fauci wrote that he "gave Jake some questions to ask" pediatrician Brett Giroir during an interview on CNN’s "State of the Union." But Tapper would later express frustration, waking Fauci up in the process.

"Tapper woke me up at 11:23 AM (I went to bed early) furius [sic] at POTUS for tweeting about the fact that Jake severly [sic] questioned Brett Giroir on SOTU CNN show today. Jake was really pissed at the craziness of it all," Fauci wrote.

Fox News' Brian Flood and Joseph Wulfsohn contributed to this report.

item.title: Philadelphia Eagles lock up Jalen Carter through 2031 with record $152M contract extension
item.description: Jalen Carter's four-year, $152 million extension makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history, surpassing Jeffery Simmons and Chris Jones.
item.content:encoded:
The national stage wasn't kind to Jalen Carter at the start of the 2025 season when we saw him get kicked out of the regular-season opener for spitting at Dak Prescott, but the start of this season is getting off on a much brighter note.

As in, a Brink's truck full of $100 notes.

That's because Carter has agreed to a four-year contract extension worth a reported $152 million with $106 million guaranteed that makes him the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history.

PATRICK MAHOMES LEAPS PAST DAK PRESCOTT AS NFL'S HIGHEST-PAID QB WITH RECORD CHIEFS EXTENSION WORTH $504.75M

The deal, negotiated by agents Drew and Jason Rosenhaus, will pay Carter $38 million in new money on an annual average basis.

The average vaults Carter past Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons ($35.2 million), and Kansas City Chiefs lineman Chris Jones ($31.75 million) as the league's only interior linemen exceeding $30 million per season.

That's, shall we say, nothing to spit at.

Carter is now under contract with Philadelphia through 2031.

The No. 9 overall pick of the 2023 draft, Carter finished second in the Defensive Rookie of the Year voting behind Will Anderson Jr.

Carter was instrumental in helping the Eagles win Super Bowl LIX to cap the 2024 season. Last year he only played in 11 games until he required shoulder surgery in both shoulders.

But he played at least 90 percent of the snaps in four of those 11 games and his 55.9 snaps per game was the most among defensive tackles.

Carter is two-time Pro Bowler and the Eagles obviously believe his best days are ahead because that's exactly what $38 million per season should deliver.

Especially in games played on the national stage.

item.title: Dakota Johnson stuns as Marilyn Monroe in first look after director doubted casting
item.description: A stunning new set photo reveals Dakota Johnson's transformation into Marilyn Monroe for Maggie Gyllenhaal's short film premiering at Venice.
item.content:encoded:
Forget Dakota Johnson — the actress looked every bit the blonde bombshell as she transformed into Marilyn Monroe.

A new set photo offered fans a first glimpse at Johnson's striking new role in "Flesh Impact." The short film, written and directed by Maggie Gyllenhaal, will premiere at the Venice Film Festival in September.

The shocking transformation is just one piece of Gyllenhaal's fresh take on the Hollywood legend.

ELLEN BURSTYN ON THE HABITS SHE GAVE UP TO STAY THRIVING AT 93 YEARS OLD

Instead of a traditional biopic, "Flesh Impact" imagines Monroe beyond the platinum hair and red lipstick, exploring the woman behind one of pop culture's most enduring personas.

Gyllenhaal first worried Johnson didn't look enough like Marilyn Monroe to play the part.

"Then I thought, ‘That’s ridiculous. Who cares?’" she told Vanity Fair. "I don’t know that anyone even really totally knows what Marilyn looks like because she’s been so commodified and made into this myth, and she’s very blurry in my mind."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

For "Flesh Impact," Johnson portrayed Marilyn Monroe at age 36, the age at which the Hollywood icon died in 1962, while Ellen Burstyn played a fictionalized older version of the blonde bombshell.

The 17-minute short film aims to explore Monroe beyond her enduring public image. Rather than being a traditional biopic, the film blends reality and imagination to examine her identity, legacy and the experience of being an actress in honor of her 100th birthday.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I’ve always been fascinated by Marilyn Monroe," Gyllenhaal said in a press release. "So, when Genesis first came to me with the idea of a celebratory project for her centennial, I knew I wanted to work together on bringing this story to life.

"With ‘Flesh Impact,’ we showcase the timeless icon we know and love through a modern lens that reclaims her story," she added.

item.title: ESPN's Dan Orlovsky weighs in on Florida coach Jon Sumrall's pedicure preferences, immediately gets roasted
item.description: Dan Orlovsky declared he's "completely against pedicures for dudes" on "Get Up," sparking backlash over his makeup and infamous end zone blunder.
item.content:encoded:
While last week's SEC Media Days saw plenty of coaches putting themselves in the spotlight with a litany of quotes, one coach from the Southeastern Conference rose above the rest.

Florida's Jon Sumrall made quite a name for himself in Tampa last week during his inaugural spin as a head coach in the SEC, creating a bit of a stink on social media with his comments regarding a reporter's cell phone going off.

Sumrall apparently wasn't done hogging the limelight, though this time it was his wife generating the headlines when she dropped the bombshell that one of the toughest coaches in the conference loves getting pedicures.

FLORIDA COACH BRINGS LAUGHS, NO FILTER AND LANE KIFFIN COMPARISON REBUTTAL TO FIRST SEC MEDIA DAYS

The internet once again reacted in kind, with fans and media members arguing both sides of the issue.

Some saw no problem with a man taking care of his feet - especially feet that used to play linebacker in the SEC - while others said the revelation that Sumrall gets his toes worked on pokes holes in his "tough guy act."

A few fans even suggested his wife was in the wrong for airing out his dirty laundry (and clean feet) and giving his rivals ammo to use against him.

One man who isn't necessarily a rival coach is ESPN analyst and former NFL quarterback Dan Orlovsky.

Orlovsky was asked about "Pedicuregate" on the show "Get Up" Tuesday morning, and the ex-Detroit Lion did not mince words.

"I have never gotten a pedicure, and I never will," said Orlovsky. "I am completely against pedicures for dudes."

ESPN PARTING WAYS WITH NFL ANALYST RYAN CLARK AHEAD OF NETWORK'S FIRST SUPER BOWL BROADCAST

Sumrall is pretty clearly a dude, so it sounds like Orlovsky is against the new Gators head coach getting a pedicure.

Orlovsky was roundly mocked by all of his co-hosts on "Get Up" during the segment, but that was nothing compared to what fans on X had in store for him.

One subset of fans - both Florida and otherwise - correctly pointed out that Orlovsky calling a guy out for getting pedicures while he wears makeup on the set of a TV show feels a tad bit hypocritical.

Another subset of fans took things on a bit more of a personal route, and brought up Orlovsky's very infamous trip out of the back of the end zone during the 2008 NFL season (a season in which the Lions notoriously completed an 0-16 campaign).

I also have to say, it is relieving that fans of teams other than the Florida Gators are hopping to Jon Sumrall's defense.

I thought I was going to have to defend this take as a massive Gator homer like that one scene in "Game of Thrones" where Jon Snow has to take on hundreds of soldiers all by himself in The Battle of the Bastards.

In all seriousness, I'm not a pedicure guy. I really don't like strangers touching me in general so that rules out massages, too.

But I am in no way going to shame a man for getting his feet taken care of.

Manicures, though? That's a different story.

I have to draw the line somewhere.

item.title: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert and pop star Madison Beer announce engagement with romantic post
item.description: Los Angeles Chargers star quarterback Justin Herbert and pop star Madison Beer announced their engagement Tuesday in a romantic post to social media.
item.content:encoded:
Regardless of what happens with the Los Angeles Chargers this season, star quarterback Justin Herbert and pop star Madison Beer have already won.

The couple announced their engagement Tuesday in a joint social media post.

"Meet my fiancé," they captioned the joint post.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The couple posted 12 pictures from the big day, the first showing them sharing a kiss.

Among the pictures in the slideshow, Herbert is shown carrying an ebullient Beer over his shoulder, while another shows him on one knee proposing to her. Another picture shows a wooden sign that read "Mr. and Mrs. Herbert."

The couple was first linked together in August 2025 when Herbert was seen with the singer on the set of one of Beer’s music videos in Los Angeles. They seemed to confirm the dating rumors when they were pictured together on the sideline of a Chargers game at SoFi Stadium in October.

CHARGERS' JUSTIN HERBERT SAYS MADISON BEER 'CHANGED MY LIFE FOREVER' IN BIRTHDAY TRIBUTE: WHO IS THE POP STAR?

The couple attended a Los Angeles Lakers game later that month and sat courtside. They went viral as Herbert blocked an errant basketball from hitting Beer.

Herbert is 28, and Beer is 27. The couple’s birthdays are just five days apart. In March, each of them posted romantic messages to the other for their respective birthdays.

Herbert is heading into his seventh season as the Chargers quarterback.

Last season, in 16 games, Herbert led the Chargers to an 11-5 record, completing 66.4% of his passes for 3,727 yards with 26 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. The former Oregon star also ran for 498 yards and two touchdowns.

He made the Pro Bowl for the second time in his career.

item.title: Leading economist warns of rise of 'Gen Z affordability socialism'
item.description: Diogo Costa says AI is transforming the economy, but support for free markets is fading as a new generation embraces 'affordability socialism.'
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is fundamentally transforming the global economy at breakneck speed, but Diogo Costa argues that the real threat to prosperity isn't technological disruption; it's the return of bad economic ideas.

As the president of FEE (the Foundation for Economic Education), America's oldest free-market think tank, Costa is concerned that the affordability crisis is providing the perfect opportunity to tempt the next generation with the ideas of socialism, and argues that economic education is the antidote.

Recently, he sat down with Fox News Digital at Freedom Fest in Las Vegas for a discussion about the intellectual defense of free markets, the intersection of freedom and technology, and how his upbringing in Brazil brings a unique perspective to today's economic policy debates.

GEN Z IS WORKING HARD, BUT THE ECONOMY IS PUTTING THE AMERICAN DREAM OUT OF REACH FOR MANY

"The biggest challenge today is the different ways that ‘anti-economics’ keeps reappearing. And this time, it's reappearing through a new kind of socialism. So through the 20th century, we had different flavors of socialism, labor union socialism, environmental socialism, anti-globalization socialism. Now we see this cost-of-living socialism, affordability crisis socialism."

While young people are aware that they are better off in a market economy, Costa argues, they still want heavy-handed intervention if they perceive it benefits them.

"Young people, they want to live in a market economy. They don't want to move to Venezuela or Cuba, but they want price controls in everything. They want to freeze the rent, they want free rides in buses, they want to make sure that groceries are either run by the government or price controlled somehow. And this is not just a phenomenon in New York City or California. This is something that's happening globally. 

"And this is the new kind of ‘anti-economics.’ So, Leonard Read [founder of FEE] understood that economics is always one generation away from turning prosperity into poverty. The good ideas need to keep being recycled, they need to be reframed, and this is a challenge that we have right now, the rise of this Gen Z affordability socialism."

He further argues that while the technology produced by vibrant market economies has incredible potential, the ideological foundation of capitalism is under attack like never before:

"We're in a golden age for technology, not necessarily for the ideas behind it…the ideas behind the market economy are not as well understood. And when you talk about AI, people are thinking all the jobs are going to be gone. Humanity is on the verge of extinction. 

"So there is a lot of pessimism at the same time that you have these wonderful technologies. So the ideas that help us explain and help us work with technology are what's missing."

Costa's studies of the Austrian school of economics lead to separating the economic power of the free-market from its cultural power:

"Joseph Schumpeter, the Austrian economist, said that capitalism would be economically powerful and at the same time culturally weak because you have companies that will be doing amazing things, but capitalism makes things more abstract…and at some point people stop seeing exactly how they are part of this amazing complexity.

DEMOCRATS LURE ‘POLITICALLY HOMELESS’ GEN Z TOWARD SOCIALISM — A COUNTERATTACK IS TAKING SHAPE

"That's why with FEE we sometimes go back to a pencil. We just ask people ‘do you understand how a pencil is made?’ Because if you see the complexity, the network, the amazing, marvelous market system around... Just building a single pencil, you start to understand how you are part of the complexity and you benefit from it."

Costa's own experience growing up in Brazil during the economically chaotic 1990s was pivotal in shaping his outlook on policy and the need for economic education.

"I grew up in a country that had hyperinflation. When I was 10 years old, 11 years old, yearly inflation was above 1000%, 1200%, 1300%. That meant the prices were changing literally every day. And it's hard to understand how if you live in a society that is that economically chaotic all your life is designed around those problems. 

"So as a child, when I was going to the grocery store because my mom gave me a $1,000 bill to buy a bag of chips, I had to think, ‘Oh, I need to get there before the price tagger starts changing the prices’."

"My parents had to turn a bedroom in our house into a pantry because when they got their paychecks the first thing they did was go to the grocery store and buy everything you can…So your life starts to be designed around these big issues. And this is something that some people take for granted."

But it was not only hyperinflation that opened Costa's eyes about economic education; he also first hand the effects of a fundamentally protectionist economic system:

"It's the same thing with protectionism…as a young boy in the early 90s, I wanted video games. Brazil had strict protectionism. So I could buy these dupe video games, but I couldn't get the real deal. And this was something that people now take for granted, but this was how the Brazilian economy was being shaped. 

"And Milton Friedman has this saying that he thinks that we never actually learn economics as humanity, we learn as individuals, we learn maybe as generations, but now that we don't live under hyperinflation people forget what that's like, now that we don't live under hyperprotectionism people forget what it's like. So it's very easy to drift towards inflation, to drift towards protectionism, to drift towards anti-economics and economics needs to be re-taught every generation."

item.title: SEE IT: Mark Kelly blames Trump's agenda for boosting AOC as Dems presidential pick
item.description: Mark Kelly says Trump's policies prioritizing billionaires over the middle class are driving Democratic voters toward Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's message.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., argued that President Donald Trump is driving Democratic voters toward far-left candidates like Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez after the New York Democrat topped a recent 2028 presidential primary poll.

A recent New Hampshire poll found Ocasio-Cortez was the top choice among likely Democratic voters for the party's 2028 presidential nomination. Kelly placed third with 9% support, behind Ocasio-Cortez and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, while ahead of California Gov. Gavin Newsom and former Vice President Kamala Harris. The poll comes as several self-described Democratic Socialists have defeated more moderate Democrats in recent primary elections, showing the growing influence of the party's progressive wing.

Kelly has teased a run for president in 2028, recently saying in an NBC interview that it is part of an ongoing discussion with his family that he has "plenty of time" to decide on.

HASAN PIKER MAKES AOC HIS 2028 PICK FOR PRESIDENT, SAYS IT'S 'NOT EVEN A QUESTION’

"I don't know about her message, but people are really struggling," Kelly told Fox News Digital about why Ocasio-Cortez was Democrats top 2028 pick.

Fox News Digital asked Kelly why Ocasio-Cortez and other candidates associated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) are resonating with the Democratic voters ahead of upcoming election seasons.

"The policies of this president — supporting billionaires over hardworking people," Kelly said. "1% of the country now owns more wealth than the middle class, and I think it's a response to that."

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

In 2021, Federal Reserve data showed the top 1% of households now hold more wealth than the bottom 60% combined for the first time since the central bank began tracking the data in 1989.

item.title: Nolan Wells mystery deepens as email indicates teen drank heavily before vanishing
item.description: A newly released Marine Patrol email listed 18-year-old Nolan Wells’ alcohol intake as “heavy” during the search for him after he disappeared on a boating trip to Horn Island.
item.content:encoded:
The mysterious death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells has taken another turn after a newly obtained document listed the missing teen's alcohol intake as "heavy" as authorities searched for him on Horn Island over the Fourth of July weekend.

The document, a July 5 Mississippi Department of Marine Resources Marine Patrol email obtained by Fox News Digital, was sent to the U.S. Coast Guard as authorities searched for Wells.

Along with his physical description and last known location, the email lists "Alcohol intake: Heavy," but does not identify the source of that information.

Wells, an Ole Miss freshman from Jackson, Mississippi, disappeared while on a boating trip to Horn Island with friends. An extensive multi-agency search ended July 6 when his body was discovered.

SEARCH CALLED OFF AFTER BODY MATCHING MISSING TEEN NOLAN WELLS FOUND OFF MISSISSIPPI COAST

Authorities have not publicly identified a cause or manner of death, and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy and toxicology results remain pending.

The newly reported details come days after a private autopsy commissioned by Wells' family concluded his cause and manner of death were "undetermined pending investigation."

NOLAN WELLS INDEPENDENT AUTOPSY DOESN'T POINT TO FOUL PLAY, FORMER MEDICAL EXAMINER SAYS

During a July 22 news conference, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said an area of "red discoloration" was found on the back of Wells' head but said Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed the independent autopsy, could not determine a cause or manner of death pending further investigation. 

"Crime Stories with Nancy Grace" host Nancy Grace later discussed the findings on her show, where she raised additional questions about the investigation.

She pointed to what she described as deep red tissue beneath the skin at the back of Wells' head and said the independent pathologist did not receive Wells' lungs or throat when conducting the second autopsy.

Grace also questioned whether those findings could be significant but emphasized that she did not know what caused Wells' death and noted there were "many accidental possibilities."

"There is deep, red, subcutaneous tissue" on the back of Wells' head, Grace said, adding that the discoloration was localized rather than consistent with postmortem blood pooling.

Grace then questioned why the lungs and throat were unavailable during the independent examination.

"When the second autopsy got the body, the lungs and the throat were missing," Grace said. "I understand why they took the lungs to determine if he had drowned, but why was the neck missing? What about the interior of the throat sparked the initial medical examiner's concern?"

She stressed that those questions remain speculative until investigators release additional findings.

"I don't know," Grace said. "There are many accidental possibilities."

The Jackson County District Attorney has defended the investigation amid growing public scrutiny, saying authorities are following standard procedures and awaiting forensic testing before drawing conclusions.

Authorities have not announced whether foul play is suspected.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Jackson County Sheriff's Office and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's Office for comment.

item.title: Folk icon Linda Perhacs reportedly missing as friends seek answers after months of silence
item.description: Linda Perhacs' friends say the 82-year-old psychedelic folk singer has been unreachable for eight months after her legal guardian discharged her from care.
item.content:encoded:
Friends of legendary folk singer Linda Perhacs are asking the public for help, claiming the 82-year-old artist went missing after leaving a residential care facility about eight months ago.

In a statement shared with Fox News Digital by Perhacs' former manager, Laurel Stearns, friends and collaborators said the acclaimed singer-songwriter was discharged from the facility under the supervision of her legal guardian and has not been heard from directly since. 

They said repeated attempts to reach both Perhacs and her guardian have gone unanswered.

MICHAEL J. FOX SAYS GOING PUBLIC WITH PARKINSON'S WAS 'HELL' ON WIFE TRACY POLLAN

"Concern is growing among friends, collaborators, and members of the music community regarding the well-being and current whereabouts of acclaimed singer-songwriter Linda Perhacs," the statement read.

According to the statement, "she was discharged from a residential care facility approximately eight months ago under the supervision of her legal guardian. Since that time, numerous friends and longtime collaborators report they have been unable to establish direct contact with her. Repeated attempts to communicate with her guardian have also, they say, gone unanswered."

Those issuing the statement emphasized they are not accusing anyone of misconduct, but rather "seeking confirmation that Linda is safe, well, and receiving appropriate care, while expressing concern over the prolonged absence of communication with a beloved public figure."

The apparent disappearance of Perhacs has prompted both an Adult Protective Services case and a police report, according to the folk icon's friends. With the investigation ongoing, additional details are being withheld.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Perhacs' friend Mark McNeill also urged the public to help locate the influential musician in an Instagram post.

"Linda Perhacs our dear friend and legendary singer-songwriter was discharged from a residential care facility approximately eight months ago under the supervision of her legal guardian… Please help us locate Linda to ensure her wellbeing."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Perhacs' decades-spanning career took an unexpected turn when her 1970 album "Parallelograms" — initially overlooked upon release — was rediscovered decades later and transformed into a cult classic. The singer-songwriter later experienced a career resurgence with the release of "The Soul of All Natural Things" in 2014 and "I'm a Harmony" in 2017.

After months without direct contact, friends said they decided to speak out in hopes of confirming Perhacs is safe and receiving appropriate care.

"As a public artist whose work has profoundly influenced musicians and listeners around the world, Linda's well-being is of genuine concern to a broad community of admirers and colleagues," the statement continued.

"Those issuing this statement respectfully request that anyone with verified information regarding Linda Perhacs' current condition or means of contact reach out to her authorized representatives or designated point of contact. The intention is not to intrude upon her privacy, but simply to ensure that she is safe and to re-establish communication with someone whose artistic contributions continue to resonate across generations."

item.title: Landon Donovan says soccer has arrived in America after record-breaking World Cup summer
item.description: With nearly 7 million fans filling stadiums this summer, Landon Donovan declares soccer is here and partners with AT&T for the MLS All-Star Game.
item.content:encoded:
The World Cup did not go exactly how the United States Men's National Team expected, but the sport was the talk of the country this summer.

Nearly 7 million people flooded stadiums in North America to catch World Cup action, and the final between Spain and Argentina peaked at 52 million viewers, averaging at around 38 million.

Landon Donovan was an analyst for FOX throughout the event and said this year's World Cup was an unforgettable memory.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I'm sad it's over now. It really did go by so fast. Maybe for people at home, not so fast. But for us, it was just travel, game, work, game, travel, appearance, travel, meet-and-greet, travel, game. It was honestly the time of my life, and I'm sad it's over," Donovan told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

"The superstars showed up and scored goals. The fan bases were incredible. The infrastructure and the stadiums, of course, are amazing in this country. The fans filled the stadiums. It broke records in every way on TV and social. It was a phenomenal World Cup, and I'm really just sad it's over."

It remains to be seen what kind of growth will occur in the U.S. after the World Cup, but if it's anything like what occurred in 1994, the sport is in a good spot – just in time for Major League Soccer's All-Star Game in Charlotte on Wednesday.

Donovan partnered with longtime MLS sponsor AT&T for the festivities to bring fans closer to the action.

"They've been supporters of ours for a long time. Soccer, to most people, is relatively new, but I've been in this game for a long time. So when you have people and companies that want to support in a real way and not just throw money at it, but actually be involved, then it means a lot to us because we've been ambassadors for this game forever," Donovan said. "They're helping us connect people to this game that we love, and that means a lot. They're great with our podcast with me and Tim Howard. Great to me personally, individually, all the All-Star Games. They love the sport. They genuinely do, and it's been really nice to have them."

IOC DECLINES TO INVESTIGATE GIANNI INFANTINO OVER TRUMP'S CALL ABOUT FOLARIN BALOGUN RED CARD

Donovan recalled the ovation he got when he returned to MLS after the 2002 World Cup.

"I lived it, right? At the end of these tournaments, there's so much energy and excitement around soccer and the sport, so you'll see an uptick in viewership. You'll see an uptick in the stadiums. People now know these guys' names, and it's a really, really awesome opportunity to grow as a player, but also to grow your brand," he said.

"When I came back in 2002, I literally got off the plane from Korea and went straight to the stadium at noon, maybe 2:00. We had a game that night, and I got to play for 10 minutes at the end of the game. The excitement in the stadium for the fans to see someone who, 24 hours earlier, had been on a field in Korea was awesome. So these guys coming back into the league a week before the All-Star Game, and then a lot of them at the All-Star Game, it's a really awesome opportunity to be recognized and appreciated. It's really cool."

While a deeper USMNT run would have done wonders for the sport, Donovan, though, is done talking about when soccer will arrive – because he thinks "soccer is here."

"There has been study after study, they asked people to name their favorite sport. The NFL was one, the NBA was two and soccer was three — soccer in general, right? So people do love this sport in this country," he said. "I know anecdotally, I drop my kids off at school every day. I don't see NFL jerseys. I don't see baseball jerseys. I see soccer jerseys. The kids are all wearing soccer jerseys. They're all in. So soccer is here.

"Now, how you quantify it in a real way via Major League Soccer or U.S. Soccer, I don't know. That's harder to do. But this sport is mainstream now. When you turned on the TV this summer, people were talking about soccer... So, it is here. It's not where we all want it to be yet, but that takes time, man. These other sports have had decades, if not centuries, of a head start on soccer. So we'll just keep going."

item.title: Ex-NHL star Ron Duguay hospitalized after losing consciousness amid Stage 4 cancer battle
item.description: Video showed Ron Duguay being taken by ambulance after fainting at home, as the former Rangers star battles Stage 4 liver cancer and internal bleeding.
item.content:encoded:
Former New York Rangers center Ron Duguay had a scary incident this past week as his daughter, Shay Thomas, revealed he fell unconscious at home and suffered injuries.

Thomas posted on Instagram Monday, where she revealed her father passed out after being "extremely dehydrated."

Duguay, who was diagnosed with Stage 4 cancer earlier this year, also had "varices, portal hypertensive gastropathy, internal bleeding, and an ulcer," after seeing doctors.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"Our dad @ronduguay10 continues to show us just how strong he is," Thomas wrote on her post on Instagram. "On Friday, he fainted at home, was unconscious, injured a few parts of his face, and knocked out a few teeth in the fall…this time, it wasn’t from hockey. He was taken by ambulance to the hospital."

Duguay’s cancer is in his liver, and Thomas revealed that "pressure has built up inside the liver" after "surgery, chemotherapy, and the pump."

"That pressure can back up into the stomach and cause bleeding. The ulcer still needs further evaluation, but the bleeding and liver pressure are the major concerns right now," Thomas added.

Thomas’ post also had video of Duguay entering the back of an ambulance on a stretcher.

"He is still admitted to the hospital and receiving blood transfusions while the doctors continue to monitor closely," Thomas wrote in her post.

"Through it all, our dad remains strong, positive, and trusting God every step of the way. We will continue to keep everyone updated. Please keep him covered in prayer."

Duguay wasn’t discouraged by the incident, saying "Found my teeth on the bedroom floor," in an Instagram Story that showed a picture of him without some teeth.

Duguay revealed his cancer diagnosis in February, issuing a heartbreaking plea for help as he pursued treatment "in hopes of giving him the best possible chance."

Duguay, 68, first opened up about his health to Page Six, telling the outlet that seeking financial support has been a challenge for him as someone who has used his platform to try to help others.

"I find it extremely hard asking for funds for all these costs I’m going through," he said. "Normally, I’m helping others."

RANGERS GREAT RON DUGUAY'S FAMILY MAKES HEARTBREAKING PLEA AS HE BATTLES STAGE 4 CANCER

Duguay was diagnosed with colon cancer more than a year ago, losing his appendix and gallbladder during his treatment as a result. His family started a GoFundMe campaign to share the details of his condition and plans for additional treatment.

"Our dad has never been someone who asks for help …especially when it comes to money. He has always tried to handle everything on his own and didn’t want to burden anyone else with what he’s going through. But after many conversations as a family, we decided to create this fundraiser for him because we’ve seen firsthand the weight this battle has placed on him, both physically and financially," the family wrote on the campaign post.

"Because of his cancer, he hasn’t been able to work the way he normally would, yet he continues to fight with everything he has. Earlier in his treatment journey, the care he received in Florida nearly cost him his life. That led us to bring him to Orange County, where my sister and I live, so he could receive treatment here … and thankfully, it has helped him so far."

Duguay was one of the Rangers’ most recognizable players of the late 1970s and early 1980s after getting drafted 13th overall in 1977. He was an instrumental part of the team’s run in the 1979 Stanley Cup Final.

He played in 864 games during an 11-year NHL career, recording 274 goals and 346 assists. He also played for the Detroit Red Wings, Pittsburgh Penguins and Los Angeles Kings.

Duguay is in a relationship with former Republican vice presidential nominee and former Alaska Gov. Sarah Palin, who has been a strong supporter of the former NHL player throughout his cancer battle.

Fox News’ Paulina Dedaj contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump reflects on infamous phone-number stunt that sparked friendship with Graham
item.description: Trump recounted how sharing Lindsey Graham's cellphone number during a live 2015 speech sparked an unlikely friendship that lasted a full decade.
item.content:encoded:
In an emotional farewell Tuesday, President Donald Trump paid tribute to the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., recounting how their relationship evolved from fierce political foes into close allies and friends.

Trump said the turning point came after he publicly revealed Graham's cellphone number during a campaign rally in Bluffton, S.C., in 2015 — a decision he acknowledged Tuesday was a mistake.

"As you remember, Lindsey and I did not exactly get off to the best of starts," Trump said during his eulogy address at the Washington National Cathedral, adding that Graham had said something "nasty" when they were both running for the 2016 presidential nomination.

"So naturally, I did something that I shouldn't have done," the president continued. "I shared his personal cellphone number with the millions of people that happened to be watching that particular day as I made a speech, a very important speech."

FROM 'DISGRACE' TO 'FAMILY': TRUMP'S REMARKABLE JOURNEY WITH LINDSEY GRAHAM

"And I remember the number (202) 228-0292 if anybody wants to give it a shot," Trump went on, sparking laughter in the room.

"His phone exploded. He said, ‘I had that number for 20 years.’ His phone totally — I don't know what he did with it. But it exploded," Trump said. "That was the beginning of a friendship, in a way."

"But it was Lindsey who had the last laugh, because while I blew up his phone all for one day, we became great friends and Lindsey did not stop calling me for the next 10 years," Trump continued.

The unlikely friendship grew to include frequent rounds of golf and late-night phone calls as Graham became a leading advocate for Trump’s legislative agenda.

Since Graham's death earlier this month, Trump has repeatedly spoken about the senator's constant presence in his life.

LINDSEY GRAHAM'S FINAL MISSION NEARS FINISH LINE AS WORLD LEADERS GATHER TO HONOR HIM

And before the service began, before the cameras began rolling, before the speeches, and before Graham’s casket arrived, the Washington National Cathedral became a gathering place for those who the late lawmaker knew, worked alongside, advocated for, and, at times, fought.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, two of Graham’s closest allies on the world stage, both attended — holding court separately among the sea of lawmakers and Cabinet members filing into the cathedral.

Much of the Senate attended, too, including Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., who wore a suit. A rare sight not seen even at Trump's second inauguration.

Meanwhile, Trump’s affection for Graham was visible throughout his remarks.

He called him a "beloved friend, a devoted brother, a respected statesman, a giant of the United States Senate, and a true American original who left us much too soon."

"For more than 30 years, nothing of consequence happened in this Capitol without Lindsey Graham knowing about it," Trump reflected. "Nothing of significance happened anywhere in the world without Lindsey Graham having a view on it. And no bill became law… without Lindsey Graham having a say in it. He was a man who gave America the full measure of his good and mighty heart."

item.title: Japan mall rebuilt after deadly 2016 earthquake destroyed in major temblor weeks after 'fresh start' reopening
item.description: A massive explosion ripped through Aeon Mall in Kumamoto just weeks after its grand reopening, leaving up to 30 employees unaccounted for.
item.content:encoded:
A shopping mall in southern Japan that had just reopened after years of reconstruction following a devastating 2016 earthquake was destroyed Tuesday after a powerful earthquake struck the region and was followed by a massive explosion, leaving dozens of workers unaccounted for.

The Aeon Mall in Kumamoto Prefecture celebrated its grand reopening on June 13 after years of rebuilding meant to mark the region's recovery from the 2016 disaster.

Just weeks later, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck near Kumamoto, according to FOX Weather, citing the U.S. Geological Survey. Japan's Meteorological Agency measured the same quake at magnitude 7.1 using its own seismic scale.

EARTHQUAKE SHAKES PERU'S ANDES REGION, KILLING AT LEAST 5, DISPLACING HUNDREDS

About 200 shoppers were safely evacuated after the earthquake, officials said. Roughly an hour later, a powerful explosion ripped through the building, blowing off exterior walls and exposing its steel framework. NHK reported that about 20 to 30 mall employees remained unaccounted for, while police said rescuers could not immediately enter because of the risk of aftershocks.

The mall had become one of the most visible symbols of Kumamoto's recovery after the magnitude 7.3 earthquake that devastated the region in April 2016. Aeon said the redevelopment included seismic reinforcements and other safety improvements designed to make the complex more resilient.

Witnesses reported smelling gas before the explosion, according to Reuters. An Aeon spokesperson said employees immediately helped evacuate visitors after the quake, while prefectural officials confirmed about 200 people were guided safely outside before the blast.

EXCLUSIVE: FRANKLIN GRAHAM VISITS EMERGENCY HOSPITAL TREATING VENEZUELA EARTHQUAKE VICTIMS

According to FOX Weather, the earthquake struck just before 4:30 p.m. local time about 9 miles north of Kumamoto at a depth of roughly 6 miles. Japan's Meteorological Agency briefly issued and later lifted a tsunami advisory for parts of Kyushu. NHK reported at least 50 people were injured, while Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency said the quake sparked at least eight fires. Kumamoto Airport also temporarily closed.

Reuters reported the mall welcomed more than 8 million visitors annually after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. opened a factory nearby in 2024.

The complex housed about 200 stores, a movie theater and parking for roughly 5,000 vehicles. It also became known locally after a supermarket inside sold 10-yen onigiri to help survivors following the 2016 earthquake.

When the mall reopened in June, Aeon described the project as a "'re-start' initiative" marking both the shopping center's 21st anniversary and the region's recovery from the 2016 earthquake.

As night fell Tuesday, rescue operations remained on hold because of continuing aftershocks as families awaited word on the employees still believed to be inside.

item.title: Soft exosuit helps people walk without bulky motors
item.description: A 4.2-pound soft exosuit using artificial muscles instead of motors cut walking energy use by nearly 14% in treadmill tests with six adults.
item.content:encoded:
Walking through an airport or around a large store can take more energy as we get older. Researchers in China are now testing a soft robotic suit that could someday help your legs do some of that work.

The experimental soft exosuit assists the hips using thin artificial muscles instead of conventional motors and gearboxes. The research, published in the peer-reviewed journal Science Advances, describes a 4.2-pound prototype that fits around the waist and thighs like a lightweight harness.

In a small treadmill test, six healthy adults used an average of 13.9% less energy while the powered assistance was active. Sensors also showed that their leg muscles worked less.

So, how does the soft exosuit actually work, and what still needs to improve before you could ever wear one?

SELF-DRESSING CLOTHES COULD HELP OLDER ADULTS

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

Many robotic exoskeletons rely on rigid motors to move a person’s joints. Others use compressed air, which requires pumps, valves and an air tank. Those components can make an exoskeleton heavy or noisy. They can also restrict how naturally your body moves.

The new soft exosuit takes a different approach. It uses flexible muscle-like fibers positioned near each hip. As you walk, the fibers pull at the right point in your stride to help move your leg forward. Straps transfer that pulling force from the artificial muscles to the wearer’s hips and thighs. The flexible design allows the suit to move with the body rather than enclosing the legs inside a rigid frame. "Motor-free" refers to the lack of traditional motors and gearboxes. The suit still uses a compact battery pack and electrical power system to activate its artificial muscles.

The artificial muscles use a rubber-like material called a dielectric elastomer. The material changes shape when exposed to an electric field. Researchers have studied dielectric elastomers for years. However, earlier designs lacked the force needed to help move a human leg. Many were also too bulky for a comfortable wearable device.

Wei Yu and his colleagues at Hebei University of Technology changed the molecular structure of the material to improve its performance. They then rolled thin layers into long fibers. Next, the team grouped several fibers into bundles. The arrangement works somewhat like human muscle, where many smaller fibers pull together to create greater force.

The researchers also created modular connectors that allow them to add more fibers when an application requires additional pulling power. According to Hebei University of Technology, the actuators completed more than 100,000 cycles during laboratory testing. Longer studies will need to show how well the materials hold up during daily wear.

COULD A PAINT-ON ELECTRONIC TATTOO SPOT HEART ATTACKS?

The researchers tested the soft exosuit on six healthy volunteers. Each participant walked on a treadmill under several conditions. They walked without the suit. They also wore it with the artificial muscles turned off. During another round, the electrical assistance actively supported their hips.

A metabolic testing system measured how much oxygen each person used. Sensors attached to their legs also tracked muscle activity. When the assistance was active, the volunteers used an average of 13.9% less energy than they used while walking without the suit. Lower muscle activity also suggested that their legs needed less effort to complete each step.

That reduction could feel meaningful during a long walk. However, this study involved a controlled treadmill setting and a very small group. The volunteers were also healthy adults. Researchers still need dedicated studies involving older people and those with mobility challenges.

A wearable device that reduces walking effort could help people stay active longer as their leg strength changes. Think about walking through a large grocery store or spending the day with family. A lightweight suit that takes some strain away from your hips could make those outings feel more manageable.

The design may also feel less intimidating than a rigid robotic frame. Its artificial muscles resemble cords built into clothing, while the supporting straps fit close to the body. People recovering from surgery could also benefit from this type of assistance one day.However, future clinical trials will need to determine who can use the suit safely and how much support each person needs. Balance presents another important consideration. The current study focused on the energy required for walking rather than fall prevention or stability.

The current prototype remains an early research system. Battery life limits how long the suit can provide assistance. The researchers want future versions to operate longer without adding much weight.

The control system also needs to respond automatically when a person speeds up or slows down. Walking across grass or climbing a slope would create additional challenges. Voltage presents another hurdle. Dielectric elastomer actuators often require more than 1,000 volts. The current stays very low, but any wearable consumer product would need strong insulation and extensive safety testing.

Researchers will also need to study how the fibers respond to sweat and changing temperatures. Repeated bending during everyday activities could affect long-term performance as well. No consumer price or release date has been announced.

FDA TO REVIEW 7 POPULAR PEPTIDES TOUTED FOR WEIGHT LOSS, HEALING AND LONGEVITY

You will not be buying this soft exosuit anytime soon, but the research shows where mobility support could be headed. A lighter system that moves with your body could feel far more natural than today's bulky powered exoskeletons.

The nearly 14% drop in walking energy use is encouraging. Still, the test involved only six healthy adults on a treadmill, so we need much more evidence about comfort, safety and real-world use.

The next big step is testing the suit with older adults and people who already have trouble walking. That is where we will learn whether these artificial muscles can truly help people stay active and independent. For now, anyone noticing changes in mobility should talk with a doctor or physical therapist about the support that makes sense today.

What grabs me here is how much walking support the researchers created without loading someone down with bulky motors. A 4.2-pound suit that cut energy use by nearly 14% is worth watching. Still, this was a very small lab test with only six healthy adults. The battery needs to last longer, and the high-voltage system will need serious safety testing. The bigger test comes next. I want to see how this soft exosuit performs with older adults on real sidewalks and over longer periods before we call it a true mobility breakthrough.

item.title: Blackburn unveils bill to keep biological men out of Daughters of the American Revolution
item.description: Sen. Marsha Blackburn's bill would amend the DAR's federal charter to require biological women membership after the group voted against a born-female rule.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX — Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., is introducing legislation Tuesday that would prohibit biological males from joining the Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR), saying the historic women's organization should be reserved for biological women.

"The Daughters of the American Revolution was founded by women for women, and its founders would be appalled that the organization is now allowing biological males to become members and undermine the legacy of real women who helped build our nation," Blackburn told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"The Daughters of the American Revolution Membership Integrity Act would amend the DAR’s federal charter to stop the organization from erasing biological reality and ensure it is reserved for the real daughters of the American Revolution," Blackburn added.

MED SCHOOL DEANS COME UP EMPTY IN TENSE HEARING WHEN ASKED POINT BLANK IF MEN CAN HAVE BABIES: 'RIDICULOUS'

Blackburn’s bill would amend the organization's federal charter to require that members be biological women, according to bill text first obtained by Fox News Digital. Blackburn's office said the legislation is intended to preserve the group's mission and ensure eligibility standards reflect its identity as a women's organization.

The bill follows similar efforts by Republicans to draw legal distinctions based on biological sex in athletics, prisons, shelters and other single-sex spaces.

Earlier this month, Rep. Ben Cline, R-Va., introduced legislation in the House that would require the DAR to limit membership to biological women, saying the historic organization's congressional charter should reflect its original mission after the group adopted a policy interpreted as allowing transgender applicants.

WASHINGTON MOTHER SAYS SHE FOUND ADULT MALE SHOWERING IN WOMEN'S LOCKER ROOM DURING CHILDREN'S SWIM MEET

Blackburn’s bill is cosponsored by Sens. Katie Britt, R-Ala., Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., Mike Lee, R-Utah, Tand Kevin Cramer, R-N.D.

The Daughters of the American Revolution, founded in 1890, is federally chartered and made up of women who are direct descendants of American Revolutionary War patriots.

The group voted 1,481 to 984 on June 26 against a measure to keep membership for those "born female," the New York Post reported.

NBC ANCHOR FORCED TO EXPLAIN USE OF TERM 'BIOLOGICAL MALE' DURING COVERAGE OF SUPREME COURT RULING

"The Daughters of the American Revolution are called ‘Daughters’ for a reason—this organization is meant to honor the legacy of American women and their ancestors, not pander to a distorted sense of reality manufactured by far-left radical Democrats," Britt told Fox News Digital in a statement. 

"Whether in women’s locker rooms or time-honored organizations like DAR, it is our job to protect women and girls in spaces that are rightfully theirs. I’m proud to cosponsor this commonsense legislation," she said.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Lee said, "It’s right there in the title: ‘DAUGHTERS’ of the American Revolution. Congress created this group in 1890 to recognize the American women preserving our history, but their D.C. chapter is now admitting biological men. The woke invasion of every feminine space has to stop – there’s already a group for Sons of the American Revolution! Our bill will reverse this needless policy to give the women who built this organization the protection and legitimacy they deserve."

Tuberville said, "There’s a reason the founders of this group named it the DAUGHTERS of the American Revolution. They had the common sense to recognize what a woman is; unlike the woke Left that apparently doesn’t understand the differences between female and male anatomy. Alabama has over 4,000 members in the DAR, and they shouldn’t have to be putting up with this woke nonsense. Amending the eligibility requirements to reflect the founders’ vision is something all of my colleagues should be able to get behind."

Cramer told Fox News Digital in a statement that the "Daughters of the American Revolution was founded specifically for women to honor our patriotic forbears."

He added, "Today’s Daughters meticulously research their genealogy to prove direct lineage to the heroes of the past, drawing inspiration from the accounts of the women who came before them. Their stories and heroism are rooted in their lives as women, and as a federally chartered organization, the Daughters of the American Revolution should reflect and honor this biological reality. Our legislation ensures membership eligibility is crystal clear."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Daughters of the American Revolution for comment.

item.title: World-famous Catholic shrine torched, 'Devil in a skirt' scrawled on Virgin Mary statue
item.description: Surveillance footage shows a man pouring gasoline on the altar at St. James Church as the Medjugorje shrine was vandalized days before a major festival.
item.content:encoded:
A man has been arrested after one of the world's most famous Catholic pilgrimage sites was vandalized and partially set on fire, with a statue of the Virgin Mary defaced and the words "Devil in a skirt" scrawled across its pedestal in black, according to reports.

Bosnian police arrested a suspect Tuesday in connection with the overnight vandalism and arson at the Shrine of Our Lady in Medjugorje, according to Vatican News.

Authorities have not released the man's identity as investigators work to determine a motive and whether he was responsible for other incidents reported at the shrine that same night, the outlet said.

NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES

Police were called around 4:30 a.m. on July 27 after the face and hands of the statue of the Virgin Mary on Apparition Hill, also known as Podbrdo, were found covered in black paint.

The pedestal at the foot of the statue was spray-painted with the English phrase "Devil in a skirt," while other graffiti and the statue's hands were painted black.

An outdoor altar nearby was also set on fire near St. James Church, the outlet said.

Surveillance footage reportedly at that location showed a man pouring what investigators believe was gasoline onto the altar before setting it ablaze. The fire was extinguished.

REPORT DETAILS RISING PRESSURE ON UNDERGROUND CATHOLICS AS CHINA DENIES CRACKDOWN

The two attacks came just days before Medjugorje's annual youth prayer festival, which is expected to draw more than 50,000 pilgrims from around the world.

In a statement Tuesday, the Medjugorje Parish Office condemned the vandalism and urged Catholics to respond with "prayer, fasting, and forgiveness" rather than anger.

"It is with great sadness that we received the news of the act of vandalism," the parish said.

Church officials also said cleanup and repairs began immediately so the damaged prayer sites could once again welcome pilgrims.

"The affected areas are being cleaned and restored as quickly as possible," the parish said, thanking volunteers for helping preserve the shrine as "a place of encounter with God, a place of peace."

CATHOLIC NUNS SUE NEW YORK, SAY ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW FORCES THEM TO VIOLATE THEIR FAITH

Rather than calling for retribution, the parish urged the faithful to pray for those responsible.

"We pray for the conversion of the hearts of those who committed this act," the statement said, asking that God "touch them with His grace and lead them on the path of goodness."

The parish also appealed for peace, encouraging Catholics "not to return evil for evil," but instead to bear witness through "love, forgiveness and hope."

Despite the attack, officials said the shrine remains open, and its regular schedule of Mass and prayer services will continue as planned.

Located about 85 miles southwest of Sarajevo, Medjugorje became one of the world's best-known Catholic pilgrimage destinations after six children and teenagers reported seeing apparitions of the Virgin Mary there in 1981.

The Vatican gave the green light for Catholics to continue flocking to Medjugorje offering its approval for devotion at one of the most contested sites of Roman Catholic practice in recent years, The Associated Press reported Tuesday.
