item.title: Trump says heroic teen lifeguard who saved boy from towering waves deserves White House honor
item.description: Trump says the California teen who repeatedly disappeared beneath crashing waves while saving a child showed extraordinary courage worthy of national recognition.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised the teenage lifeguard who went viral after rescuing a young boy from towering waves in Santa Cruz, California, saying he wants to invite the teen to the White House and potentially award him a high civilian honor.

The lifeguard, identified as 16-year-old Ryder on social media, was captured in a heart-stopping video Saturday battling massive surf as he repeatedly disappeared beneath crashing waves while maintaining a relentless grip on the child he was rescuing.

After seeing the dramatic rescue, Trump said the teen deserved national recognition. 

"We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor. Very brave, he deserves it!" Trump said in a post on X. 

HEROIC 16-YEAR-OLD LIFEGUARD RESCUES CHILD FROM MONSTER SURF IN HEART-STOPPING VIDEO

The Santa Cruz State Lifeguard Association (SCSLA) confirmed to Fox News Digital that its lifeguard did an "excellent job" during the rescue, praising him for saving a life.

Hours earlier, Eric Trump also praised the rescue on social media, calling for the teen to receive the nation's highest civilian recognition. 

"Give this 16-year-old lifeguard the highest civilian honor. This is truly the best of America! Well done!" he said. 

The rescue drew thousands of reactions online, with many praising Ryder for battling powerful waves that appeared too dangerous even for bystanders who attempted to help. 

One person claiming to have witnessed the rescue said it lasted far longer than the viral video showed. Beachgoers reportedly formed a human chain in an effort to help before it was eventually broken apart by the pounding surf, according to social media users. 

MAN, WOMAN KILLED IN RIP CURRENT AS LIFEGUARD SHORTAGE LEAVES DANGER ZONES IN BEACH DESTINATION

After pulling the child safely onto the beach, Ryder reportedly sprinted past his lifeguard tower to get aid as paramedics arrived to evaluate the boy, the witness said. Despite the dramatic rescue, Ryder later returned to duty and continued watching over beachgoers for the rest of the evening. 

The rescue may have come during Ryder's first season as a lifeguard. California State Parks requires state lifeguards to be at least 16 years old.

Another social media user who said she knew Ryder emphasized how extraordinary the rescue was. 

"I’m not sure how many people know how hard it is to hold onto someone like that in the ocean, during these heavy conditions and pounding shore break. This lifeguard handled it like a pro, pulled him in most of the way solo and never gave up. That is a feat in itself, especially in those conditions. A true Hero & waterman. I seriously hope he gets recognized for this," the user said. 

Other people claiming to have witnessed the incident said the surf had initially appeared relatively calm, with many beachgoers standing at the water's edge when a massive wave suddenly crashed ashore. 

"It was so big it nearly reached us by our things all the way up the beach!" the witness said. 

Seabright Beach is known for its powerful shore break, with waves shaped by swells arriving from multiple directions, creating hazardous conditions even for experienced swimmers.

item.title: Hot bobsledder Desi Johnson gets in touch with nature, ‘Shark Lady’ breaks world record & woke brewery busted
item.description: NFL training camp is here, Minocqua Brewing Company loses its permit, and bobsledder Desi Johnson escapes to Kyrgyzstan for a nature retreat.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

It's a beautiful day, Nightcaps family.

You know why? I'll tell you. Because as of today, Tuesday, July 28 in the Year of our Lord 2026, all 32 NFL teams have reported to Training Camp.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That means in just a couple short weeks (well, one week if you count the Hall of Fame Game), preseason football will be on our TV screens. And shortly afterward, college ball will consume our Saturdays. As God intended.

Not trying to wish away anyone's summer — my colleagues Joe Kinsey and SeanJo would be very disappointed in me if I did that — but MAN. Call me Hank Jr. because I am ready for some football.

Speaking of summer, I'm still in Minocqua, Wisconsin, at my mother-in-law's house. Nashville feels like the devil's sweaty armpit this time of year, so it's nice to get a little bit of cooler weather up here in the Northwoods.

Last week, we shot up to the Minnesota North Shore for some hiking. Goodness, it's beautiful up there. And they have some great local breweries, too.

My dog is way too cool for his own good.

But you didn't come here for my family photos. You came to find out what's going on on the internet today. So let's get to it, shall we?

Pop open a Fulton 300 IPA, chuck your work laptop into Lake Superior and let's go.

An update on the wackos at Minocqua Brewing Company

Speaking of beer...

If you've been reading my Nightcaps for a while, you might remember me talking about the Minocqua Brewing Company. It's "downtown" Minocqua (I'm using that term loosely) inside an old gas station from the 1930s.

Actually, a pretty cool little building. Perfect spot for a brewery. Shame the owner, Kirk Bangstad, is a certified nutcase.

Now, I pride myself in my ability to get along with people who don't agree with me, but I assure you Kirk has no desire to get along with me. Or likely anyone reading this, for that matter.

He's as far left as they come. There are signs plastered all over the outside of the joint that say "least popular place in town," "drink MAGA tears" and "Antifa parking only."

The beers are named things like "AOC IPA," "The Resistance," "Choice," "Fascist Tears" and their Mexican lager, "It'll Always Be the Gulf of Mexico to Me." They also sell their own coffee and coffee stout, called "WOKE."

To their credit, that's actually a pretty clever name for coffee.

I digress. This guy isn't insufferable because he's a lib. I know lots of libs, and I like them just fine. He's insufferable because he's awful.

Kirk is always at war with the city and other local businesses, and he's been charged with multiple legal offenses, including criminal defamation, harassment, bail jumping, disorderly conduct, and (last but not least) defrauding donors to his super PAC by funneling thousands of dollars to himself to pay for his legal fees. Last year he tried to hijack the 4th of July parade. I don't have the time or patience to list his whole rap sheet.

But if it tells you anything, this dude is such a turd he even named one of his beers after his lawyer. It has the guy's face on the can and everything. 

Well, this week, his permit got pulled. Turns out, Kirk has been illegally transporting beer from Illinois without securing the proper permits or paying the appropriate taxes.

Not paying taxes! Imagine that.

The revocation is effective Aug. 4 — next Tuesday. Still, he has no intention of shutting down.

"They’ll have to pry me out of my taprooms before I stop selling beer to thirsty progressives who come to visit us," he wrote, per the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.

So I'll be sure to walk by the brewery today and wave to ol' Kirk before he likely gets hauled off by the authorities.

I'm sure his lawyer, Fred Melms (aka "Grateful Fred Red Ale") will be on the case.

Bobsledder Desi Johnson gets in touch with nature

I'm not the only one escaping the hustle and bustle of the city. Desi Johnson — a Team Australia bobsledder who went viral during the Winter Olympics for being hot, as one does — got away on a nature retreat in rural Kyrgyzstan this week.

Gotta admit, Kyrgyzstan is not a country I've ever thought twice about. Or once, actually. But it looks beautiful.

I have no idea what the bobsledding season looks like. As far as I know, people only bobsled once every four years. But I'm sure there's some sort of training or competitions involved in the interim.

Regardless, Desi seems to be keeping busy traveling, getting outdoors, running sprints and selling workout clothing.

Someone's ready for French Alps 2030!

'Shark Lady' breaks record for most shark tattoos

Hold on, let me clarify: She has broken the world record for "most sharks tattooed on the body (female)" with 106.

I know what you're thinking: Amber, does that mean some dude out there has 107 shark tattoos?

And the answer is no. Or if he does, he hasn't come forward. I guess the folks over at the Guinness Book of World Records wanted to specify female body just to leave the door open for a man who wanted his own shot at glory.

I swear there is a Guinness World Record for everything. Somewhere out there, someone just broke the world record for "most Busch Lights (corn can) drank in a northern Illinois garage on an overcast Monday in July."

And yes, I have one specific person in mind for that one.

SHARK WEEK HOST FORREST GALANTE EXPLAINS WHY CRUSHING BEERS IN THE OCEAN IS A BAD IDEA

True story, though, remember a couple of weeks ago when I was telling y'all about the mountain of dumb PR pitches that end up in my email inbox daily?

Case in point: I got an email from an organization (a movement? a nonprofit? a cult? I truly have no idea) called "World Clap Day" — proudly announcing that its founder, Andrea, completed 24 consecutive hours of live clapping, setting a new world record. That's 149,216 claps!

I bet her hands hurt so bad.

You know, when I first read that email, I thought to myself, Why in the hell would these people think I would write about this? And here I am, writing about it.

Touché, clapping cult.

Wow, I really got in the weeds there. Back to the shark tattoo chick.

Her name is Emily Morrison, and she goes by "Shark Lady Emily" on social media.

A fitting moniker, to be sure.

And don't you dare try to tell Emily to stop getting shark tattoos. Because you know what she has to say about that?

"I will not stop getting shark tattoos."

If you're really into this sort of thing, Emily will be featured on My Strange Addiction as part of Discovery's "Shark Week."

I've only watched that show one time, and it was an episode about a lady who can't stop eating toilet paper. So when you look at it that way, Emily's actually killing it.

item.title: Minnesota Vikings suspend defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander after DWI guilty plea
item.description: Gerald Alexander's blood alcohol level was more than twice the Minnesota legal limit, leading to a guilty plea and and a three-week team suspension.
item.content:encoded:
Another NFL assistant coach is being disciplined by his team after facing driving under the influence allegations, this time with Minnesota Vikings defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander being suspended by the team.

The Vikings announced Tuesday that Alexander has been suspended for three weeks after he pleaded guilty to driving while intoxicated earlier this month. Alexander's blood alcohol level was 0.169, or more than twice Minnesota's legal limit, on an initial breathalyzer test, according to the charging statement.

Alexander, hired in February as the team's passing game coordinator as well as defensive backs coach, was arrested in April, and his guilty plea came on July 16.

NFL SUSPENDS ARIZONA CARDINALS EXECUTIVE FOR VIOLATING GAMBLING POLICY, LEAKING DRAFT INFO

Alexander pleaded guilty to third-degree DWI, a misdemeanor, and paid $603 in fines and fees. He was assigned 48 hours of community service and will be on probation for two years.

Alexander's club suspension began on July 24, although it was not announced then. It will run through Aug. 13.

"Following Gerald’s arrest earlier this spring, we remained in communication with the NFL while awaiting the outcome of the legal process," the Vikings said in a statement. "We take these situations seriously and believe this disciplinary action is appropriate."

The NFL tells Fox News Digital the club suspension will close the matter and Alexander will not be subject to additional league discipline under the personal conduct policy.

Alexander, who previously worked under Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores in Miami when Flores was the head coach, also released a statement through the team.

"I take full responsibility for the situation I put myself in and apologize for not meeting the mark," Alexander said. "I know it’s unacceptable. I understand the suspension and am committed to learning from the matter and ensuring I come back a better version of myself."

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

Alexander is the second NFL assistant coach to face team discipline for offseason troubles with DWI.

The Washington Commanders on Monday announced the firing of assistant coach Ben Steele just days before the start of training camp.

Steele, who was serving as the team's tight ends coach, was hired by the Commanders this offseason.

"We are parting ways with tight ends coach Ben Steele. The team will have no further comment at this time," the Commanders said in a statement.

The Athletic reported that Steele was arrested on suspicion of DWI in June. He is facing an additional charge for refusing a blood/breath test and obstructing or resisting an officer without force, per the report.

Steele had previously been under suspension by the Commanders.

These two issues coming to light in the same week suggest some coaches may need more extensive training or onboarding to make clear the pitfalls of drinking — even away from the club.
